You will also support the integration and validation of externally supplied optical payloads, working with internal engineering teams and external suppliers to ensure successful integration into the satellite platform. The role requires a strong background in spacecraft AIT, system integration, or complex hardware integration, combined with the ability to lead people, coordinate technical activities, develop robust processes, and drive execution in a fast-paced production environment. Who We Are ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth. ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system. ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. DESIGN MATURITY AND CO-ENGINEERING - Work with Engineering from the concept phase so that design and production constraints are aligned, applying design for manufacturing, assembly and testability (DFM, DFA, DFT) and bringing harness routing, connector access, test points and diagnostic provisions into internal design iterations before the design is frozen. - Support internal and supplier design and readiness reviews (e.g. PDR, CDR, PRR, IRR, TRR), ensuring designs are mature and ready for transition into production, and identify industrial risks early with the action plans that close them. ELECTRICAL INTEGRATION AND ASSEMBLY - Own the integration readiness of the satellite electrical subsystems, including avionics, power, data handling and communications. - Lead and execute electrical integration of satellites and sub-assemblies: harness routing and connection, electrical and RF connections, connector handling, grounding and bonding. - Own the electrical build standard, including crimping and soldering practice, connector identification, continuity and insulation verification, cleanliness and ESD discipline. - Perform and oversee in-house PCB assembly and rework according to defined work packages and workmanship standards. - Verify electronic assemblies before integration and support the floor hands-on during build, connection and test setup. FUNCTIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL TEST - Plan, prepare and lead functional, interface and performance test campaigns at subsystem and satellite level, and support the electrical side of environmental campaigns including EMC, thermal vacuum and vibration. - Develop and maintain automated and semi-automated test scripts, and monitor telemetry and telecommand during test execution. - Act as first responder for electrical anomalies during integration and test, performing initial diagnosis with laboratory instruments and taking findings to root cause. You will work across the Portuguese Portfolio focusing on the technical thread of customer missions—from requirements capture through system acceptance and delivery—acting as the technical authority/interface between the customer and ICEYE's engineering, product, and operations teams. Your role bridges program governance and system engineering: ensuring mission requirements are understood, flowed down, tracked, and validated, while maintaining configuration control and driving cross-functional technical alignment throughout the program lifecycle. This role directly contributes to ICEYE's ambition to become the leading provider of space-based ISR infrastructure by scaling reliable, high-impact mission delivery globally. The role will be based in Lisbon at the ICEYE facility. Travel to customer sites is required. WHAT WILL YOU DO IN THIS ROLE? ICEYE is seeking a Mechanical AIT (Assembly, Integration & Testing) Engineer to own the mechanical side of production end to end -- integration, testing, supplier selection, continuous improvement, and adapting processes as new designs come through. In this role, you will be the technical expert responsible for satellite mechanical integration and vibration testing, ensuring that the structure, payload, solar arrays, propulsion and thermal hardware come together as a flight-ready unit that survives launch. You will act as the primary technical contact for mechanical integration issues and drive improvements in build cycle time, test efficiency and build reliability, ensuring every spacecraft meets ICEYE’s high standards for reliability and mission success. Key Responsibilities - Lead the mechanical integration of the satellite (structure, payload, solar arrays, propulsion, harness routing, thermal hardware), including torque control, bonding, alignment and mass properties measurements - Own vibration test campaigns end to end: test specification, fixtures, instrumentation, execution, data analysis and reporting, with test levels and FEM correlation defined together with Structures Engineering - Act as primary technical contact for mechanical integration issues, performing root cause analysis on nonconformances and coordinating with Mechanical/Structures Engineering to resolve anomalies - Survey, evaluate and select suppliers and test facilities for mechanical parts, MGSE and fixtures, including audits and first article inspections - Contribute to and improve AIT documentation, including mechanical integration procedures, test plans and as-built configuration records - Interface with Global AIT, Mechanical/Structures Engineering, QA and Launch teams to ensure alignment on product standards and lessons learned - Drive continuous improvement and automation in mechanical integration methods, test data processing and build cy
